basics.name: Kyle M. Anderson
basics.summary: Software Development Manager and backend developer with 6+ years of experience designing, developing, and maintaining enterprise integrations and API-driven applications. Experienced in integrating ERP, financial, e-commerce, and tax systems using REST/SOAP APIs. Background includes API architecture, database development, performance optimization, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, and technical project leadership.

work.name: DSTax Technologies
work.summary: As Development Manager, I remained actively involved in backend development and integration architecture while coordinating development initiatives and client implementations.
highlights: Developed integrations between financial platforms and tax providers, including Acumatica, Chargebee, Sage Intacct, WooCommerce, Magento/Adobe Commerce, Thomson Reuters, Vertex, Sovos, and SureTax.
Supported end-to-end integration implementations, including requirements gathering, setup, troubleshooting, and go-live support.
Led the transition from Version 1 to Version 2 of the tax-integration platform
Optimized asynchronous operations to improve performance and throughput.
Migrated production infrastructure from DigitalOcean to AWS, supporting the continued operation and scalability of integration services.
Created and maintained client guides and knowledge-base articles.
broadening tax-provider and financial-platform support and improving UI/UX.

work.name: Colectivo Coffee Roasters
highlights: Partnered with the IT department to install and troubleshoot new point-of-sale nodes.
Updated invoices for inventory changes to help maintain accurate records.

work.name: Komatsu Mining Corp. (Joy Global)
highlights: Initiated web automations that reduced manual database-maintenance work.
Managed SharePoint sites and data and designed data-input forms to improve accessibility, reduce errors, and promote cross-department information sharing.
Evaluated, selected, and implemented a global mapping platform that provided facility information to employees and customers.
Analyzed asset and facilities databases, identifying more than $10 million in previously unidentified asset value that informed the sale of unused assets before Komatsu's acquisition of Joy Global.
